If destination is not an existing directory like when renaming something, destination is the new file name. But we want to move into archives directory. We can first cd into archives then mv temp_notes.txt notes_2024.txt? But temp_notes.txt is in parent directory. We can use mv with source temp_notes.txt and destination archives/notes_2024.txt? But the tool says no path allowed. So we need to cd into archives, then mv temp_notes.txt notes_2024.txt? But temp_notes.txt is not in archives. So we need to move from parent to archives. We can use mv with source temp_notes.txt and destination notes_2024.txt after cd into archives? That would move from archives to archives? Not correct. We need to move from current directory to archives. The tool's description: "Move a file or directory from one location to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax. type mv = (_: { source: string, destination: string, }) => any; // Source name of the file or directory to move. Source must be local to the current directory. // The destination name to move the file or directory to. Destination must be local to the current directory and cannot be a path. If destination is not an existing directory like when renaming something, destination is the new file name."

Thus we cannot specify a path. So we cannot move into archives directly. We might need to use cp then rm? But cp also cannot specify path. So we cannot move into subdirectory. But maybe we can cd into archives then mv temp_notes.txt notes_2024.txt? But temp_notes.txt is not in archives. So we can't. So maybe we need to use cd to archives, then mv ../temp_notes.txt notes_2024.txt? But source must be local to current directory. So cannot use relative path. So we cannot move into archives. But maybe we can use cp to copy to archives? But cp also cannot specify path. So we cannot. So maybe we need to use rmdir? No.

Thus we cannot accomplish this with the given tool constraints. We can explain that.')
